Solution B
Step 1

The problem wants us to test whether the mean number of complaints per airport is less than 151515 per month. In making assumptions, let us recall the condition before conducting a hypothesis. These conditions should be checked first to make sure that the results are reliable. We will also need to make a frequency distribution table to show that the information given can be used in testing a hypothesis. Finally, if the previous questions are answered positively, we can proceed to test the hypothesis.

Step 2

(a) Assumptions

Before conducting a test hypothesis, we need to assume that we will be working on data from a population following a normal distribution.

Step 3

(b) Plot of the Number of Complaints per Airport:

Here, we construct a dot plot to represent the frequency of the number of complaints per airport. In the information given, there is 111 airport with 101010 complaints, 444 airports with 121212 complaints each, 555 airports with 131313 complaints each, 555 airports with 141414 complaints each, 333 airports with 151515 complaints each, and 222 airports with 161616 complaints each. Showing this information in a dot plot we have:

By just looking at the obtained dot plot, the frequency distribution of the samples follows a bell curve-like pattern.

Since the random sample collected is from the population, we can say that it is reasonable to say that the population also follows a bell curve shape which also indicates a normal distribution.

Step 4

(c) Testing of Hypothesis:

Null and Alternate Hypothesis

Our goal is to answer whether the mean number of complaints per airport is less than 151515 per month. Thus, our null hypothesis is that the population mean is at least 151515 complaints while the alternate hypothesis is that the population mean is less than 151515 complaints. We can express these hypotheses as:

H0: μ≥15H1: μ<15\begin{aligned} H_{0}:\ \mu\geq 15\\ H_{1}:\ \mu<15 \end{aligned}H0​: μ≥15H1​: μ<15​

Here, we will use a one-tailed test because we only want to know whether there has been a decrease in the number of complaints. Now, look at the inequality of the alternate hypothesis. Since it is less than, then the region of rejection is in the left tail of the distribution.

Step 5

Test Statistic

In part (b) we confirm that the distribution follows a normal distribution. Also, we do not know the variance of the population, thus we will use the left-tailed t−t-t−distribution. The value of test-statistic, when population standard deviation is unknown, can be calculated by:

t=x‾−μsnt=\dfrac{\overline{x}-\mu}{\frac{s}{\sqrt{n}}} t=n​s​x−μ​

where x‾\overline{x}x is the sample mean, μ\muμ is the hypothesized population mean, sss is the sample standard deviation, and nnn is the number of observations in the sample.

Step 6

Decision Rule

To formulate the decision rule, we need to use the table for the critical values of ttt for the one-tailed test. To locate the critical value ttt, we first determine the degrees of freedom (dfdfdf). This value is the difference between the total number of observations and 111. In the information given, there are 202020 samples. Thus,

df=20−1=19df=20-1=19 df=20−1=19

The first column of the table shows the degrees of freedom and the first row shows the confidence interval. The value at row 191919 (degrees of freedom) and column 0.050.050.05 (level of confidence) is 1.7291.7291.729 but because our rejection region is on the left side of the distribution, then we will take the negative of the value shown. Hence, our critical region is −1.729-1.729−1.729. Therefore, the decision rule is to reject H0\boldsymbol{H_{0}}H0​ if the value of t\boldsymbol{t}t is less than −1.729\boldsymbol{-1.729}−1.729.

Step 7

Decision

Now that we have a decision rule, we proceed to calculating ttt. We know that our n=20n=20n=20 for there are 202020 observations, and the hypothesized population mean is 151515 then μ=15\mu=15μ=15. We do not know the sample mean and the sample standard deviation yet so we compute for the two values using the formulas:

x‾=Σxn                      s=Σ(x−x‾)2n−1\overline{x}=\dfrac{\Sigma x}{n}\ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ s=\sqrt{\dfrac{\Sigma(x-\overline{x})^{2}}{n-1}} x=nΣx​                      s=n−1Σ(x−x)2​​

Sample Mean:

x‾=Σxn=14+14+16+⋯+13+10+1320=27020=13.5\overline{x}=\dfrac{\Sigma x}{n}=\dfrac{14+14+16+\cdots+13+10+13}{20}=\dfrac{270}{20}=13.5x=nΣx​=2014+14+16+⋯+13+10+13​=20270​=13.5

Sample Standard Deviation:

s=Σ(x−x‾)2n−1=(14−13.5)2+(14−13.5)2+⋯+(10−13.5)2+(13−13.5)220−1=(0.5)2+(0.5)2+⋯+(−3.5)2+(−0.5)219=0.25+0.25+12.25+0.2519=4319=2.2632=1.5044\begin{aligned} s&=\sqrt{\dfrac{\Sigma(x-\overline{x})^{2}}{n-1}}\\[0.8em] &=\sqrt{\dfrac{(14-13.5)^{2}+(14-13.5)^{2}+\cdots+(10-13.5)^{2}+(13-13.5)^{2}}{20-1}}\\[0.8em] &=\sqrt{\dfrac{(0.5)^{2}+(0.5)^{2}+\cdots+(-3.5)^{2}+(-0.5)^{2}}{19}}\\[0.8em] &=\sqrt{\dfrac{0.25+0.25+12.25+0.25}{19}}\\[0.8em] &=\sqrt{\dfrac{43}{19}}\\[0.8em] &=\sqrt{2.2632}\\[0.8em] &=1.5044 \end{aligned}s​=n−1Σ(x−x)2​​=20−1(14−13.5)2+(14−13.5)2+⋯+(10−13.5)2+(13−13.5)2​​=19(0.5)2+(0.5)2+⋯+(−3.5)2+(−0.5)2​​=190.25+0.25+12.25+0.25​​=1943​​=2.2632​=1.5044​

Step 8

We can now proceed to calculating ttt by substituting x‾=13.5,μ=15,s=1.5044,n=20\overline{x}=13.5,\mu=15,s=1.5044,n=20x=13.5,μ=15,s=1.5044,n=20 into the ttt formula:

t=x‾−μsn(Write the formula.)=13.5−151.504420(Substitute the values.)=−1.51.50444.4721(Evaluate the square root.)≈−4.4590(Simplify.)\begin{aligned} t&=\dfrac{\overline{x}-\mu}{\frac{s}{\sqrt{n}}}&&(\text{Write the formula.})\\[1.5em] &=\dfrac{13.5-15}{\frac{1.5044}{\sqrt{20}}}&&(\text{Substitute the values.})\\[1.5em] &=\dfrac{-1.5}{\frac{1.5044}{4.4721}}&&(\text{Evaluate the square root.})\\[1.5em] &\approx-4.4590&&(\text{Simplify.}) \end{aligned}t​=n​s​x−μ​=20​1.5044​13.5−15​=4.47211.5044​−1.5​≈−4.4590​​(Write the formula.)(Substitute the values.)(Evaluate the square root.)(Simplify.)​

Since the computed ttt value is −4.4590-4.4590−4.4590, then we reject the null hypothesis because −4.4590-4.4590−4.4590 is less than the critical value −1.729-1.729−1.729 and −4.4590-4.4590−4.4590 falls into the rejection region.

Solution A
Step 1

First step is to state the null hypothesis and the alternative hypothesis. It asked to conclude that a larger proportion of men were driving on the New Jersey Turnpike π\piπ than the national statistics indicate which is 0.520.520.52, thus, it will be the alternate hypothesis H1H_1H1​. Then the null hypothesis H0H_0H0​ be the opposite of the statement, it will be the smaller or equal proportion of men were driving on the New Jersey Turnpike than the national statistics indicate. The hypothesis will be

H0:π≤0.52H1:π>0.52\begin{aligned} H_0 &: \pi \le 0.52\\ H_1 &: \pi > 0.52\\ \end{aligned}H0​H1​​:π≤0.52:π>0.52​

Step 2

Second step is to set the significance level. Based on the given, the significance level will be at

α=0.01\alpha = 0.01 α=0.01

Step 3

Third step is to select a test statistic, since the problem is in the assumption of non-parametric test and it needs to compare the proportion of men driving in Turnpike and the national statistics indicate. Thus, it needed to use the one proportion as testing for the hypothesis. The test statistic formula will be

z=p−ππ(1−π)nz = \frac{p-\pi}{\sqrt{\dfrac{\pi(1 - \pi)}{n}}} z=nπ(1−π)​​p−π​

where:

  • ppp is the sample proportion,
  • π\piπ is the population proportion, and
  • zzz is the test statistic
Step 4

Fourth step is to formulate the decision rule. In order to accomplish, it needed to find the critical value. Since the curve is one-tailed where the rejection region is on the right side of the curve, then the total area for the right side is 0.50000.50000.5000 subtracting it by the significance level α\alphaα is 0.010.010.01. Thus,

0.5000−0.01=0.490.5000 - 0.01 = 0.49 0.5000−0.01=0.49

Next is to look 0.490.490.49 or closes to it on the table of the area under the normal curve. It will be:

11z  ⋯0.03⋯⋮⋱⋮2.3⋯0.4901⋮\begin{array}{|c|ccc|} \hline \phantom{\frac{1}{1}}z~~&\cdots&0.03&\cdots\\ \hline \vdots&\ddots&\vdots\\ 2.3&\cdots&0.4901\\ \vdots&\\ \hline \end{array}11​z  ⋮2.3⋮​⋯⋱⋯​0.03⋮0.4901​⋯​

The row will be 2.32.32.3 and the column is 0.030.030.03, adding the row and the column to find the critical value. Thus,

z=2.3+0.03=2.33\begin{aligned} z &= 2.3 + 0.03\\ &= 2.33 \end{aligned}z​=2.3+0.03=2.33​

Since the critical value is obtained, the null hypothesis is fail to be rejected when the test statistics is less than or equal to the critical value 2.332.332.33. The decision rule will be

When z > 2.33, reject H0.\text{When z > 2.33, reject~} H_0. When z > 2.33, reject H0​.

Step 5

Fifth step is to make a decision. To accomplish it, compute the test statistic by substituting the population proportion π\piπ is 52%52\%52%, sample size nnn of 300300300, sample proportion of 0.56670.56670.5667 into the formula of one-sample proportion test. Thus,

z=p−ππ(1−π)n=0.5667−0.520.52(1−0.52)300=1.61903119≈1.62.\begin{aligned} z &= \frac{p-\pi}{\sqrt{\dfrac{\pi(1 - \pi)}{n}}}\\ &= \frac{0.5667 - 0.52}{\sqrt{\dfrac{0.52(1-0.52)}{300}}}\\ &= 1.61903119 \approx 1.62. \end{aligned}z​=nπ(1−π)​​p−π​=3000.52(1−0.52)​​0.5667−0.52​=1.61903119≈1.62.​

Step 6

Since the test statistic is less than the critical value

1.62<2.33.1.62 < 2.33. 1.62<2.33.

Then the null hypothesis is fail to be rejected. The decision will be

Fail to reject H0.\text{Fail to reject } H_0. Fail to reject H0​.

Step 7

Sixth step is to interpret the result. Based on the result of the test, it suggested that it cannot be concluded that the proportion of men driving on the Turnpike is larger than the national statistics indicate which is 0.520.520.52.

(c) Not detecting an increase in the population mean is called a type II error.

The probability of a type II error can be decreased by:

Increasing the sample size (because having more information about the population will allow us to make better estimations).

Increase the significance level (because this increases the probability of making a Type I error and decreases the probability of making a Type II error).

Making the alternative proportion ppp more extreme (thus ppp greater than 0.77, since more extreme alternatives are easier to prove).

x‾=329+503+505+...+44980=3602380=450.2875\overline{x}=\dfrac{\begin{matrix}329+503+505+...+449\end{matrix}}{80}=\dfrac{36023}{80}=450.2875 x=80329+503+505+...+449​​=8036023​=450.2875

The variance is the sum of squared deviations from the mean divided by n−1n-1n−1. The standard deviation is the square root of the variance:

Step 7

(c) Given:

n=Sample size=80x=Number of successes=28α=Significance level=0.01\begin{align*} n&=\text{Sample size}=80 \\ x&=\text{Number of successes}=28 \\ \alpha&=\text{Significance level}=0.01 \end{align*}nxα​=Sample size=80=Number of successes=28=Significance level=0.01​

Given claim: ppp is less than 40%

The claim is either the null hypothesis or the alternative hypothesis. The null hypothesis states that the population proportion is equal to the value mentioned in the claim. The alternative hypothesis states the opposite of the null hypothesis.

H0:π≥40%=0.40H1:π<0.40\begin{align*} H_0&:\pi \geq 40\%=0.40 \\ H_1&:\pi < 0.40 \end{align*}H0​H1​​:π≥40%=0.40:π<0.40​

If the alternative hypothesis HaH_aHa​ contains <<<, then the test is left-tailed.

If the alternative hypothesis HaH_aHa​ contains >>>, then the test is right-tailed.

If the alternative hypothesis HaH_aHa​ contains ≠\neq=, then the test is two-tailed.

Left-tailed test\text{Left-tailed test} Left-tailed test

The rejection region of a left-tailed test with α=0.01\alpha=0.01α=0.01 contains all z-scores below the z-score z0z_0z0​ that has a probability of 0.01 to its left.

P(z<z0)=0.01P(z<z_0)=0.01 P(z<z0​)=0.01

Let us determine the z-score that corresponds with a probability of 1−0.5−0.01=0.491-0.5-0.01=0.491−0.5−0.01=0.49 in the normal probability table of the appendix (the z-score z0z_0z0​ is then the negative of this z-score). We note that the probability 0.49 is closest to 0.4901, which is given in the row starting with "2.3" and in the column starting with ".03", thus the corresponding z-score is 2.3+.03=2.332.3+.03=2.332.3+.03=2.33.

z0=−2.33z_0=-2.33 z0​=−2.33

Thus the rejection region then contains all z-scores smaller than −2.33-2.33−2.33 and thus we reject H0H_0H0​ when the z-score is smaller than −2.33-2.33−2.33.

The sample proportion is the number of successes divided by the sample size:

p^=xn=2880=0.35\hat{p}=\dfrac{x}{n}=\dfrac{28}{80}=0.35 p^​=nx​=8028​=0.35

Determine the value of the test-statistic:

z=p^−ππ(1−π)n=0.35−0.40.4(1−0.4)80≈−0.91z=\dfrac{\hat{p}-\pi}{\sqrt{\dfrac{\pi (1-\pi )}{n}}}=\dfrac{0.35-0.4}{\sqrt{\dfrac{0.4(1-0.4)}{80}}}\approx -0.91 z=nπ(1−π)​​p^​−π​=800.4(1−0.4)​​0.35−0.4​≈−0.91

When the value of the test statistic is in the rejection region, then we reject the null hypothesis H0H_0H0​:

z=−0.91>−1.96⇒ Fail to reject H0z=-0.91>-1.96\Rightarrow \text{ Fail to reject }H_0 z=−0.91>−1.96⇒ Fail to reject H0​

There is not sufficient evidence to support the claim that less than 40 percent of the buses are old.

P-value

The P-value is the probability of obtaining a value more extreme or equal to the standardized test statistic zzz, assuming that the null hypothesis is true.

Since the test is left-tailed, the P-value is the probability that the z-score is smaller than z=−0.91z=-0.91z=−0.91.

P(z<−0.91)P(z<-0.91) P(z<−0.91)
